text:
The existence of Threi Cut in year one established a site held by the Sworn Men of Laehiford, but in year twenty-four, the Sworn Men demanded tribute from the Griwick Compact and were refused. This refusal prompted Sou Dra to begin conspiring against Math Ham, the ruler of the Sworn Men of Laehiford, in year thirty-two. After five years, the conspiracy was uncovered in year thirty-seven, leading to Sou Dra’s expulsion from the faction for plotting against the seat. His removal immediately inspired Paernrom Sir to conspire against Thurnean Kourn, who had succeeded Math Ham in year twelve, beginning his plot in year forty. That conspiracy lasted only two years before being uncovered in year forty-two, resulting in Paernrom Sir’s expulsion from the Sworn Men of Laehiford.

The ousting of Paernrom Sir triggered a legitimacy crisis that caused Threi Cut to rise against the Sworn Men of Laehiford in year forty-two. In response, the faction spent fifty silver to buy goodwill in year forty-three, but the gesture failed to restore trust. The instability culminated in year forty-four when Raneith Meispol challenged and defeated Thurnean Kourn for leadership, taking the seat through a coup. This seizure of power caused Voudreirn Wer to win Leimmil Theall away from the ruler in year forty-seven. Four years later, in year forty-nine, Sou Dra murdered Raneith Meispol at Laehiford.

The assassination created a vacuum that led Sothkel Sald to contest Lethsel Troldmirn’s claim to the Sworn Men of Laehiford based on the rule of succession by the strongest. The dispute divided the faction in year forty-nine, with Lethsel Troldmirn carrying off three places as the Sworn Men of Hadale. This fragmentation prompted Heth Fal to begin conspiring against Sothkel Sald in year fifty. However, Heth Fal’s designs came to nothing because his target was already dead.

This refusal prompted Sou Dra to begin conspiring against Math Ham of the Sworn Men of Laehiford in 32. After five years, the conspiracy was uncovered in 37, leading to Sou Dra’s expulsion from the faction for plotting against the seat.

In 40, Paernrom Sir began conspiring against Thurnean Kourn of the Sworn Men of Laehiford. His plot was uncovered two years later in 42, resulting in his expulsion. Consequently, Threi Cut rose against the Sworn Men of Laehiford in 42 with a legitimacy of 20. The faction attempted to buy goodwill for 50 silver in 43 but failed. In 44, Raneith Meispol challenged and defeated Thurnean Kourn, taking the seat through a coup. Three years later, in 47, Voudreirn Wer won Leimmil Theall away from the ruler of the Sworn Men of Laehiford.

Two years after that, in 49, Sou Dra murdered Raneith Meispol at Laehiford. Sothkel Sald contested Lethsel Troldmirn’s claim to the Sworn Men of Laehiford based on the rule of the strongest following this death. The faction divided, with Lethsel Troldmirn carrying off three places as the Sworn Men of Hadale. In 50, Heth Fal began conspiring against Sothkel Sald, but his designs came to nothing because Sothkel was already dead.

This plot was discovered in 42, resulting in Paernrom Sir’s removal from the Sworn Men of Laehiford.

The expulsion of Paernrom Sir triggered a rebellion at Threi Cut against the Sworn Men of Laehiford in 42. The faction’s legitimacy collapsed, forcing them to spend 50 silver to buy goodwill in 43, a gesture that failed to restore trust. In the same year, Raneith Meispol challenged and defeated Thurnean Kourn for leadership, taking the seat by coup in 44. Three years later, in 47, Voudreirn Wer won Leimmil Theall away from the ruler of the Sworn Men of Laehiford. This defection enabled Sou Dra to murder Raneith Meispol at Laehiford in 49, killing the faction’s ruler.

The death of Raneith Meispol sparked a contest for succession between Sothkel Sald and Lethsel Troldmirn under the rule of the strongest. In 49, Lethsel Troldmirn carried off three places from the Sworn Men of Laehiford to join the Sworn Men of Hadale, dividing the faction. The following year, in 50, Heth Fal began conspiring against Sothkel Sald. However, Heth Fal’s designs came to nothing because his target was already dead.

The existence of Threi Cut in year 1 established a site that would later provoke conflict. In year 24, the Sworn Men of Laehiford demanded tribute from the Griwick Compact and were refused. This refusal triggered a chain of internal instability within the Sworn Men of Laehiford. In year 32, Sou Dra began conspiring against Math Ham, the leader of the Sworn Men of Laehiford. After five years, the conspiracy was uncovered in year 37, leading to Sou Dra’s expulsion from the faction for plotting against its seat.

The removal of Sou Dra created a vacuum that Paernrom Sir exploited. In year 40, Paernrom Sir began conspiring against Thurnean Kourn, the new leader of the Sworn Men of Laehiford. The plot was uncovered two years later in year 42, resulting in Paernrom Sir’s expulsion. This loss of legitimacy prompted Threi Cut to rise against the Sworn Men of Laehiford in year 42. Desperate, the faction spent silver to buy goodwill in year 43, but the gesture was rejected. The weakened position allowed Raneith Meispol to challenge and defeat Thurnean Kourn in year 44, seizing the seat through a coup.

Raneith Meispol’s rule was short-lived due to shifting alliances. In year 47, Voudreirn Wer won Leimmil Theall away from the ruler of the Sworn Men of Laehiford. Exploiting this isolation, Sou Dra had Raneith Meispol murdered at Laehiford in year 49. His death triggered a contest for leadership between Sothkel Sald and Lethsel Troldmirn under the rule of the strongest. In year 49, Lethsel Troldmirn took three places to form the Sworn Men of Hadale, dividing the original faction. This division spurred Heth Fal to begin conspiring against Sothkel Sald in year 50. However, Heth Fal’s designs came to nothing because Sothkel Sald was already dead.

In the year 4, a famine struck Vea Lode, a site held by the Sworn Men of Laehiford, leaving thirty dead and grain supplies critically short. The crisis persisted through the following years, with the death toll rising to thirty-five in the second year as twenty more inhabitants abandoned the location. By the third year, although the number of deaths fell to twenty, another twenty people left Vea Lode.

The hardship continued into the fifth year, recorded in the year 8, when ten more perished and a further twenty departed. The hunger at Vea Lode finally passed after five years, concluding in the year 9. Throughout this period, the Griwick Compact remained seated at Griwick, operating under its rule of succession by the strongest.

The Famine of 4 began in year 4 at Vea Lode, where a grain shortage resulted in thirty deaths. The crisis persisted through year 5, claiming thirty-five lives and driving twenty residents to abandon the site. In year 6, the toll remained severe with twenty additional fatalities and another twenty departures.

After a two-year interval, the famine continued into year 8, causing ten more deaths while twenty others left Vea Lode. The hunger finally passed in year 9, concluding after five years of scarcity. The Griwick Compact, which determined succession by strength, is noted among the powers of this era but no direct interaction with the famine at Vea Lode is recorded.

The Griwick Compact rose in year 4 by raiding Kebarrow during a famine at Vea Lode, seizing grain and killing twenty-eight. It soon declared war on the Wurn League over Threi Cut, defeating them at that site and taking Laehiford from their control. The conflict lasted three years before exhaustion forced peace. During this period, the Compact raided Hadale and Meigate, while its own ruler Pouldrir Ho was killed by Math Ham in year 13. Reweld Wul then took power through strength, only to be murdered by Math Ham two years later. Turaer Danpa succeeded him but was also killed by Math Ham, who had returned from exile. Kei Leassel won the subsequent contest for leadership and ruled until his death in year 17.

Under Kei Leassel’s successor Thold Valmaer, internal violence continued as Math Ham murdered him in year 20. The Compact fractured when Math Ham seized two places to form the Sworn Men of Laehiford. Heillvar Maer took the main seat but was killed by Teapeall Heampim, leading to a succession crisis where Befu Seirn won. Bu Rumpirn murdered Seirn and ruled until Wilwound Ska assassinated him in year 27. Thurnean Kourn defeated Ska in a coup and held power through year 31, when the Compact took Hadale from the Wurn League after a new war. However, Hadale broke away as the Hadale Republic in year 34. Drarka Draernthun then assumed leadership but was cast out for attempting to murder Math Ham.

Thres Thrild succeeded Draernthun in year 36, binding the Compact to the Hadale Republic through marriages in years 37 and 38. His rule ended when Durnrin Drar murdered him in year 39. Voudreirn Wer won the ensuing contest for leadership. In year 40, the Sworn Men of Laehiford declared war on the Compact over a long-held grievance and captured Griwick. The Griwick Compact was finished as a landless power, its last twelve followers scattering. A peace was made with the Sworn Men of Laehiford in year 41, but the Compact itself had ceased to exist.

Turaer Danpa assumed control of the Griwick Compact in 14 following the death of Reweld Wul at Griwick. During his brief tenure, the Wurn League purchased grain from the Compact, and the two polities established terms of trade with the Kebarrow Compact. The political landscape shifted when Kei Leassel secured the allegiance of Leimmil Theall from the Compact’s leadership.

In 15, Kei Leassel initiated a conspiracy against Turaer Danpa. Concurrently, Beirn Naem successfully persuaded Befu Seirn to defect from the ruler of the Griwick Compact. Math Ham subsequently murdered Turaer Danpa at Griwick, ending his rule.

Following the assassination, Kei Leassel contested Beirn Naem’s claim to the seat of the Griwick Compact under the succession rule of strength. Kei Leassel prevailed, taking the seat while Beirn Naem was cast out of the Compact.

Turaer Danpa assumed control of the Griwick Compact in 14 following the death of its previous ruler, Reweld Wul, who was killed by Math Ham at Griwick. During this initial year, the Wurn League purchased grain from the compact, and diplomatic terms of trade were established between the Griwick Compact and the Kebarrow Compact. Turaer’s hold on power was immediately contested when Kei Leassel began conspiring against him in 15, a move that coincided with Beirn Naem successfully winning Befu Seirn away from the compact’s influence.

The stability of Turaer’s rule collapsed later in 15 when Math Ham murdered him at Griwick. Following this assassination, Beirn Naem claimed the seat of the Griwick Compact under its succession laws, but Kei Leassel contested this claim. In the ensuing dispute, Kei Leassel successfully overturned Beirn Naem’s claim and took the seat, resulting in Beirn Naem being cast out of the compact.
In year 49, Sou Dra murdered Raneith Meispol at Laehiford. This act resulted in the death of the ruler of the Sworn Men of Laehiford.

In 44, the Sworn Men of Laehiford underwent a violent succession when Raneith Meispol challenged and killed the incumbent ruler Thurnean Kourn at Laehiford, seizing the seat by coup. The faction’s internal stability was further shaken by the exile of Drarka Draernthun after his failed attempt on Veillpea Dourn was traced to a prior grievance, while externally they publicly slighted the Kebarrow Compact despite continuing to sell grain to them. Political realignments occurred across the region as Paernrom Sir returned from exile to serve the Hadale Republic, and two marriages bound the powers together: Fouthgo Souldsound wed Ror Rim, linking the Hadale Republic to the Kebarrow Compact, while Theaki Houl married Ta Poveil at Hadale. Amidst these shifts, the Hadale Republic’s raid on Threi Cut was beaten off, and Throll Kell won Draes Wild away from the ruler of the Hadale Republic.

In 44, the political landscape shifted as Nael War, captain of the Sworn Men of Laehiford, died in Laehiford, and Raneith Meispol challenged Thurnean Kourn for leadership of that power. Following his victory over Kourn, Meispol seized the seat of the Sworn Men of Laehiford through a coup and killed Kourn at Laehiford. Concurrently, Drarka Draernthun’s failed attempt on Veillpea Dourn, traced to an earlier grievance, resulted in his expulsion from the Sworn Men of Laehiford for attempted murder. Diplomatic ties were forged when Fouthgo Souldsound married Ror Rim, binding the Hadale Republic to the Kebarrow Compact, while Theaki Houl married Ta Poveil at Hadale. Within the Hadale Republic, Paernrom Sir returned from exile to take service, and its raid on Threi Cut was beaten off. Meanwhile, the Sworn Men of Laehiford publicly slighted the Kebarrow Compact, though it purchased grain from them earlier in the year. In Kebarrow, Bundtir Thri was raised to steward, while Drearnvol Tedoul assumed the same role within the Sworn Men of Laehiford, and Throll Kell won Draes Wild away from the ruler of the Hadale Republic.
